text: Replacement goes on all the time. The outer layer of your skin and the lining of your small intestine are continually worn away, and typically replaced by cells made by mitosis, with the same genetic information as the cells they replace. Repair is replacement after damage. In a skin cut, mitosis supplies replacement cells; where needed, the daughter cells then differentiate into specialised types. The same genes don't by themselves decide what a cell becomes, and some cells specialise and stop dividing; a mature human red blood cell has no nucleus and cannot divide. Which cells do the dividing? Stem cells, next.
